briefing.briefing: Right now, the two biggest forces driving gold are a weakening US dollar and rising geopolitical tension — both of which typically push gold higher. The dollar (measured by the DXY index, which tracks the dollar against a basket of major currencies) is sitting near multi-month lows at 98.97, reportedly weighed down by nerves around US government debt levels (Reuters, ~6 hours ago). A weaker dollar makes gold cheaper for foreign buyers, which tends to increase demand and lift prices. On the geopolitical side, multiple headlines over the last 7–9 hours have flagged escalating tension around new US sanctions on Iran — unscheduled, fast-moving news like this often sparks 'safe haven' buying, meaning investors rush into gold when they feel anxious about global stability. Gold has already responded, hitting a 3-month high according to Reuters just 3 hours ago. All of this points to a BULLISH [upward-leaning] bias for gold — the trend is up, the dollar is under pressure, and fear is in the air. Confidence is 6/10 because there are two big wildcards: first, the calendar shows no scheduled events today (the data field is empty), but markets are clearly bracing for upcoming US inflation data AND a speech from the Fed Chair [the head of America's central bank] — these events are NOT listed with specific times in today's data, so treat this session as event-risk territory. Second, a rate-hike probability of 20% for the next Fed meeting on September 16th is a meaningful headwind for gold — if any speaker today sounds hawkish [in favour of keeping rates high or raising them], gold could pull back sharply. What would flip this bullish view bearish: a strong dollar bounce, hawkish Fed commentary, or a surprise de-escalation in Iran tensions. The 14-day Average Daily Range [the typical daily price movement] is 101.3 points, and today has already used 64.9 of those points, meaning roughly 36 points of average move remain — so chasing a breakout aggressively right now carries more risk than entering on a pullback [a dip back toward a recently tested price level]. Key levels to watch: any clean pullback toward the 4,600–4,610 zone would be the highest-quality area to look for a long [buy] entry on the 5M chart using ICT methodology — specifically, watch for a liquidity sweep [a brief dip below a recent low to grab stop-losses before reversing] followed by a bullish displacement [a sharp move upward]. During London and early New York, favour buy setups only — do not fight the trend by looking for shorts. Use reduced position size [trade smaller than usual] given the event risk around the Fed Chair speech; treat this as a 50–60% conviction session, not a full-size day. Screenshot this: Gold is at a 3-month high, the dollar is weak, and Iran tensions are simmering — buy the dips, not the peaks, and keep size small until the Fed Chair speaks.
